newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - July 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Sri Lankan political and business stories prepared for Reuters by NewsWatch, Colombo Tel/Fax: 94-1-735182 Internet: lucien@eureka.lk.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch
for their accuracy.
DAILY NEWS
MILK PRODUCTION AFFECTED BY HIGH TAXES

Sri Lanka's milk producing cooperatives have complained that high taxes on milk products were running them out of business as they are being forced raise prices. They said higher prices were likely to affect sales and thereby reduce earnings of some 58,000 families who depend on milk for livelihood.
LANKADEEPA
BOMB ATTACK ON BUDDHIST TEMPLE
A petrol bomb that was thrown at a Buddhist temple on Tuesday damaged part of the building and severly burnt a monk. Police said it was not immediately known who had thrown the bomb.
VIRAKESARI
SECURITY TIGHTENED AT TRINCOMALEE HARBOUR

The number of cargo ships entering the eastern Trincomalee harbour have been restricted as part of tightened security. Harbour sources said that they have been directed to allow only one ship at a time for loading or unloading.
THINAKARAN
MOSLEM CONGRESS WANTS SAFEGUARDS IN ELECTION LAW

The Sri Lanka Moslem Congress has asked the Justice and Constitutional Affairs Ministry to create a number of smaller electorates as part of election reforms to ensure that minorities got due representation in elected bodies. Sri Lanka is discussing election reforms as part of a draft constitution.
THINAKARAN
PUBLIC HELP REQUESTED TO APPREHEND ARMY DESERTERS

The Sri Lankan army has requested the public to assist in apprehending deserters. The amnesty offered to deserters ended last Saturday and 4,205 of them reported for duty during the amnesty period, it said.
DINAMINA
CHIEF SUSPECT IN MOHAROOF KILLING ARRESTED
Police arrested the main suspect in the killing of Trincomalee District MP Mohammed Mohroof on Tuesday. They said a special team had been deployed to arrest others after the suspect's interrogation.
SIX NEW TRAINS ON THE COASTLINE FROM AUGUST 1
Six new trains will be added from August 1st to the existing
coastline rail service to strengthen the existing schedule in an attempt to satisfy crying commuter needs, Transport Minister A.H.M. Fowzie said.
BANK UNION TO DISCUSS PAY RISE WITH TREASURY
The Ceylon Bank Employees' union will hold another round of discussion with the Treasury on Wednesday for a salary increase for bank employees.
POST AND TELECOMMUNICATION UNION THREATENES STRIKE
The Post and Telecommunication Officers Union has decided to take trade union action against a proposal to make postal department a corporation.
